substantive_evidence: The multiplier P=-(RiRj) is the orthogonal gradient projection in Euclidean vector L2, with norm1. Applying actual scalar Riesz–Thorin to Lebesgue times finite counting measure, followed by finite vector-norm comparison, gives Dp=d^(1/2-1/p)C4^theta tending to1; this is sufficient to choose p>2 with kDp<1 for every fixed contrast k=(M-m)/(M+m)<1. Complex endpoint extensions agree on common dense inputs.

The two-space Neumann series gives the same distributional limit for F in L2 intersect Lp. The L2 gradient field minus the projected right side is curl-free and divergence-free; Fourier projection kills it, so no unproved higher-p solution is assumed to identify the solution.

For v=chi(u-u_mean), the distributional product rule has exactly div(gamma(u-u_mean)grad chi)+g, g=gamma grad u dot grad chi; testing the original equation with chi gives integral g=0. The zero integral is indispensable for the L2 tail in dimension2.

Near the compact support, truncated gradPhi belongs to Lr for r<d/(d-1). The equation1+1/p=1/2+1/r is compatible with p<2d/(d-2), while d2 has no finite upper constraint. At infinity subtracting gradPhi(x) integral g yields |x|^(-d)||g||1, integrable to both powers2 andp. Sobolev/Poincare control the other forcing term. The final norm is uniform in gamma and depends only on the fixed geometry and ellipticity.

substantive_evidence: The quadratic K-functional minimization gives coefficient weight t squared w/(1+t squared w); integrating t^-2dt produces w^(1/2). The finite chart maps G,L have bounds at0 and1 and LG=identity, so the half-order retraction argument is valid. The Fourier difference integral gives the chart Slobodeckij seminorm, including cutoff terms. Constants are quotiented globally, not separately on each boundary component.

In boundary-normal coordinates, tangential difference quotients use admissible weak Neumann tests. The coefficient/cutoff commutators are controlled by the H1 energy bound; a^tt bounded below recovers two normal derivatives. At higher orders the differentiated coefficient terms have lower order, and isolating repeated normal derivatives gives a finite induction with nested collars. This is an actual local homogeneous-Neumann proof, not a citation to an unproved arbitrary-order boundary regularity theorem.

The Rellich vector field is supported in the gamma=1 collar, has outer normal trace, and vanishes on its inner edge. Its boundary flux is |grad_M u| squared-|f| squared. The energy bound and trace quotient normalization therefore control the full H1 trace. Smooth-flux approximation applies estimates to differences for the SAME gamma, so convergence proves the L2-flux claim uniformly.

The difference u_gamma,F-u_1,F has zero weak Neumann data and is harmonic in the collar; its representative is H1-bounded by the flux norm. The collar estimate plus the explicit one-dimensional trace bound controls every integer chart norm. Applying(1-Delta_M)^k and Parseval gives all required spectral integer exponents.

Self-adjointness gives both coefficient estimates wi^(-q/2)wj^(-1/4) and its transpose. Their geometric mean is(wiwj)^(-q/4-1/8); arbitrarily large integerq yields every L. Extra mean-zero zero eigenmodes on disconnected boundary have w=1 and cause no failure.

Its solution has homogeneous Neumann data and is harmonic near the boundary, so its boundary Hk norm is uniformly bounded by||v||2. Testing against the background Neumann mode yields coefficient decay wj^(-k/2); taking the L2 dual norm gives the claimed interior L2 decay without negative-order-flux solution regularity.

The coefficient correction has right side(1-gamma)grad u_background supported in Omega-prime. Coercivity bounds its global L2 gradient by the already rapidly decaying background interior norm. The two Neumann energy identities give b_ij=integral(gamma0-gamma)grad u_gamma,j dot conjugate grad u_gamma0,i. Holder1/q+2/p=1 gives q=p/(p-2)>2 and simultaneous arbitrary rapid decay in i,j.
